# UVEITIS

Most cases are non-infectious. Most infectious cases are associated with a

pathogen causing systemic or central nervous system infection. Diagnosis of

uveitis usually must be made presumptively due to the technical difficulty of

sampling the uvea. Cases have been associated with fungi, bacteria, viruses, and

protozoa like Toxoplasma gondii.

# For treatment of posterior uveitis (retinitis) or acute retinal necrosis (ARN)

# due to Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) or herpes simplex virus (HSV) or

# Cytomegalovirus (CMV)

[VZV or HSV retinitis and ARN](orzid2-gmenu-retinitis)

[CMV retinitis and ARN](orzid2-gmenu-abx-cmv-retinitis)

# Treatment of uveitis involves treating the underlying infection and is usually

# systemic. Refer to specific pathogen recommendations for treatment of underlyin

# infection. Contact Ophthalmology and/or Infectious Diseases for assistance.
